name: The Lily Room
concept: The current brand, elevated: a deep plum-brown room, cream type, dusty-rose details and white lilies, set like a luxury hotel welcome.
signature: oversized high-contrast serif wordmark across the hero with a fine script-like italic 'by Bita' beneath
numbered chapter eyebrows with a short rose rule before each section
treatment menu set like a hotel card: categories, hairline rules, price placeholders right-aligned
imagery: still life of white lilies and hydrangea on deep plum, soft window light, skin-texture close-ups without identifiable faces
why: Keeps the plum-and-cream identity patients know, with the polish of a luxury hotel.

name: Cover Story
concept: An editorial magazine cover for natural beauty: big serif headline, issue-style index of treatments, cream paper and an oxblood accent.
signature: headline set across the full width in two lines, second line in grey, with a 'contents' list of treatment categories opposite
founder story laid out as a magazine feature with a pull quote of the signature line
FAQ as a numbered 'reader questions' column
imagery: calm editorial portraits of skin and hands, cream backdrops, natural daylight; Bita's portrait as a clearly marked placeholder
why: Feels like a beauty editor recommended her: credible, calm and quietly luxurious.

name: Soft Arches
concept: Gentle arch shapes and sage calm: a reassuring, nurse-the-nerves first visit for people new to injectables.
signature: full-radius arch masks on the hero photo, the founder portrait and treatment cards
hairline three-step 'your first visit' row with large serif numerals, right under the hero
price list as ruled rows grouped by unit, syringe, vial and session
imagery: soft daylight, botanicals, linen and stone textures, calm close-ups of skin; sage and cream tones
why: Puts first-timers at ease by explaining the consultation before anything else.

name: Precision Grid
concept: 'Precision, respect and intention' as a design system: a Swiss grid, hairline rules, numbered treatments and one calm teal.
signature: 12-column grid made visible with fine rules; every treatment numbered like a specification
neuromodulator / filler / regenerative comparison table with units, areas and what to expect
two-tone headlines where the second clause drops to grey
imagery: clean, bright, high-key images of the treatment room and products, precise crops, no people as stand-ins for patients
why: Shows medical expertise and transparency without feeling cold or clinical.

name: Cherry on Top
concept: The signature line made visual: a confident wine-red brand world with blush pink, a cherry motif and friendly luxury.
signature: 'you, with the cherry on top' as the giant centred hero line with a small drawn cherry mark
cherry mark reused as list bullets and section dividers
blush cards on wine-red for each treatment category
imagery: bold colour-blocked still lifes in reds and blush; cherries, silk, petals; warm studio light
why: Turns her signature line into a memorable brand that feels friendly, never stiff.

name: Golden Hour
concept: Warm, sunlit portraits in large rounded photo windows: natural radiance and the glow after a good appointment.
signature: full-width photo windows inset 12px from the page edge for hero, treatments and closing call
manifesto headline with small inline pill-shaped photos between the words
warm amber accent used only on booking actions
imagery: golden-hour light on skin, sun through linen, warm diverse skin tones in close crop (mood images, never labelled as patients)
why: Sells the feeling patients want: rested, glowing and still themselves.

name: Dear Patient
concept: A personal letter from Bita: ivory stationery, ink-blue serif, handwritten-feeling warmth and a first-person welcome.
signature: hero written as a letter: 'Hi, I'm Bita!' salutation, short note and a signature line
stationery details: ruled margins, a postmark-style 'by appointment only' stamp
FAQ as 'notes before your visit' with clear timing rules
imagery: few, quiet images: paper, flowers on a desk, Bita's portrait placeholder framed like a photo clipped to the letter
why: Leads with Bita herself, so trust starts before the first appointment.

name: Hydrangea Night
concept: A dark botanical evening: deep forest green, lavender hydrangea tones and elegant italic serif, quiet luxury for returning patients.
signature: headings that split into upright sans and a lavender italic serif tail
image masks mixing a tall arch, a circle and a soft rectangle across sections
dark treatment cards with lavender hairlines and price placeholders
imagery: hydrangea and lily close-ups on deep green, low evening light, dewy textures
why: Feels exclusive and calm, made for patients who want a long-term provider.

name: Blush Studio
concept: A modern beauty studio: blush and clay tones, rounded sans type, product-like treatment cards and a friendly, contemporary voice.
signature: treatment categories as product-style cards with brand names (Xeomin, Dysport, Daxxify, Sculptra) and areas
bento grid mixing a quote, the consultation steps and a Chicago waitlist card
two-line centred headlines with the second line in clay
imagery: soft blush backdrops, product-free flat lays of tools and skincare textures, rounded crops
why: Approachable and modern for newcomers, with treatments explained like a clear menu.

name: Atelier
concept: A quiet art-gallery atelier: taupe walls, black type in a refined grotesk, one chocolate accent and generous white space; every face treated like a portrait.
signature: hero as a gallery wall: three framed images of different sizes with museum-style captions
headline split over two lines with the second line indented to form a step
treatments listed like an exhibition index with numbers and short captions
imagery: black-and-white and muted-colour portraits of texture, flowers and the studio; framed with white mats and captions
why: Matches her 'every face treated with intention' promise with a calm, artful feel.
